"""Fresh disclosed equity supply predicts short-horizon execution pressure.

Mechanism: newly reported net equity issuance is a supply shock whose market
impact can persist while shares are distributed and absorbed.  Net repurchases
have the opposite effect by reducing tradable float.  The signal only reacts
when the point-in-time accounting field changes, then decays causally over the
subsequent few trading days.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _fresh_supply_pressure(
    net_issuance: pd.DataFrame, market_cap: pd.DataFrame
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causally retain fresh issuance disclosures with exponential decay.

    A fundamental field is a point-in-time step function.  A change from the
    prior bar identifies its availability-date update; zero observations after
    that event make EWM recursion decay rather than repeatedly count a stale
    quarterly value.  Positive net issuance is adverse, so the returned value
    is negated to make buybacks score positively.
    """
    safe_cap = market_cap.where(market_cap > 0.0)
    scaled = (net_issuance / safe_cap).clip(-0.25, 0.25)
    prior = net_issuance.shift(1)
    fresh = net_issuance.notna() & (prior.isna() | net_issuance.ne(prior))
    event = scaled.where(fresh, 0.0).fillna(0.0)
    pressure = event.ewm(halflife=3.0, adjust=False).mean()
    return -pressure


@register_factor
class FreshEquitySupplyExecutionPressure(BaseFactor):
    """Short recent issuance pressure and long recent buyback supply relief."""

    factor_id = "fresh_equity_supply_execution_pressure"
    name = "Fresh Equity Supply Execution Pressure"
    category = "other"
    description = (
        "Cross-sectional rank of recently disclosed net stock issuance scaled "
        "by market capitalization and exponentially decayed from the filing "
        "update date; positive scores denote recent net repurchases."
    )
    window_length = 12
    inputs = ["close", "netStockIssuance", "marketCap"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        supply_relief = _fresh_supply_pressure(
            data["netStockIssuance"], data["marketCap"]
        )
        signal = rank(supply_relief).fillna(0.0)
        return signal.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Fresh Equity Supply Execution Pressure
programs.trading_idea: Freshly disclosed net equity issuance creates a mechanically persistent supply overhang: issuance-related shares are often distributed, hedged, or absorbed gradually rather than fully priced on the filing date. Conversely, disclosed net repurchases reduce effective float and can generate a short-lived demand imbalance. The hypothesis is falsified if stocks with larger newly reported issuance-to-market-cap subsequently outperform, or if the return differential vanishes immediately after disclosure; the edge can persist because filing-based supply information is infrequent, heterogeneous in interpretation, and costly for arbitrageurs to trade across a broad small- and mid-cap universe.
programs.description: Detects a point-in-time update in reported net stock issuance, scales the disclosed issuance or repurchase by market capitalization, and carries the event forward with a short causal exponential decay. High values represent recently disclosed net buybacks; low values represent recently disclosed equity issuance.

programs.code:
"""Idiosyncratic attention-gap reversal with a fundamental-news veto.

Mechanism: a high-volume opening gap that fails to retain its direction is more
likely to be transient attention or auction inventory pressure when it is
idiosyncratic to the sector and is not accompanied by a fresh fundamental
surprise. Sector-common moves and disclosed earnings-news moves are more likely
to contain durable information and are therefore explicitly downweighted.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _sector_mean(panel: pd.DataFrame, sector: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cross-sectional sector mean using static labels known at the bar date."""
    labels = sector.ffill().iloc[-1].reindex(panel.columns)
    labels = labels.fillna("__UNKNOWN__")
    return panel.T.groupby(labels).transform("mean").T


def _fresh_release_score(
    eps_surprise: pd.DataFrame,
    revenue_surprise: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Scale point-in-time disclosure changes by each name's trailing update size.

    A quarterly field is stepwise; its positive-lag difference is nonzero only
    when a newly available value replaces the preceding disclosed value.
    """
    eps_change = eps_surprise.diff(1).abs()
    rev_change = revenue_surprise.diff(1).abs()

    eps_scale = eps_change.rolling(252, min_periods=20).mean().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    rev_scale = rev_change.rolling(252, min_periods=20).mean().replace(0.0, np.nan)

    eps_impulse = (eps_change / eps_scale).clip(0.0, 5.0).fillna(0.0)
    rev_impulse = (rev_change / rev_scale).clip(0.0, 5.0).fillna(0.0)
    return (eps_impulse + rev_impulse).clip(0.0, 6.0)


@register_factor
class IdiosyncraticGapAttentionFundamentalVeto(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "idiosyncratic_gap_attention_fundamental_veto"
    name = "Idiosyncratic Attention-Gap Reversal"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Reverses high-volume, weakly retained opening gaps only when their "
        "size is idiosyncratic relative to the sector and no fresh earnings or "
        "revenue-surprise disclosure is detected."
    )
    window_length = 252
    inputs = [
        "open",
        "high",
        "low",
        "close",
        "volume",
        "sector",
        "epsSurprise",
        "revenueSurprise",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].replace(0.0, np.nan)
        open_ = data["open"].replace(0.0, np.nan)
        high = data["high"].replace(0.0, np.nan)
        low = data["low"].replace(0.0, np.nan)
        volume = data["volume"].fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0.0)

        gap = open_ / close.shift(1) - 1.0
        gap_vol = gap.rolling(60, min_periods=20).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        standardized_gap = (gap / gap_vol).clip(-5.0, 5.0)

        sector_gap = _sector_mean(standardized_gap, data["sector"])
        idiosyncratic_share = (
            (standardized_gap - sector_gap).abs()
            / standardized_gap.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ).clip(0.0, 1.0).fillna(0.0)

        daily_range = (high - low).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        close_location = ((close - low) / daily_range).clip(0.0, 1.0).fillna(0.5)
        retention = np.sign(gap) * (2.0 * close_location - 1.0)
        weak_retention = ((1.0 - retention) / 2.0).clip(0.0, 1.0)

        volume_base = volume.rolling(20, min_periods=10).mean().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        abnormal_volume = (volume / volume_base - 1.0).clip(0.0, 3.0).fillna(0.0)
        salience = (standardized_gap.abs() / 2.0).clip(0.0, 2.5).fillna(0.0)

        release_score = _fresh_release_score(
            data["epsSurprise"],
            data["revenueSurprise"],
        )
        fundamental_veto = 1.0 / (1.0 + release_score)

        reversal_direction = -np.sign(gap).fillna(0.0)
        signal = (
            reversal_direction
            * salience
            * abnormal_volume
            * weak_retention
            * idiosyncratic_share
            * fundamental_veto
        )
        return rank(signal.fillna(0.0))
programs.name: Idiosyncratic Attention-Gap Reversal
programs.trading_idea: The parent’s weak-retention, high-volume gap appears most useful as a state variable rather than as a universally tradable reversal. This child isolates gaps that are idiosyncratic relative to their sector and have no contemporaneous earnings or revenue-surprise update, making them more likely to reflect attention-driven auction imbalance rather than genuine common or fundamental information. The edge should persist because traders cannot reliably distinguish temporary opening-demand imbalance from private-information flow using daily bars, while attention and execution constraints delay the correction. This hypothesis is falsified if idiosyncratic, non-fundamental weak-retention gaps do not reverse more strongly over six days than sector-common or fresh-fundamental gaps.
programs.description: Ranks the signed reversal of unusually large, high-volume, weakly retained opening gaps, weighted toward gaps that are large relative to the sector move and vetoed when a fresh earnings or revenue surprise is present.

"""R&D-conditioned intangible productivity realization.

Mechanism: R&D acceleration is an economically meaningful state only when an
intangible-heavy firm converts that investment into coherent improvement in
gross profit, operating margin, and cash generation. The signal scales the
productivity-realization spread by the firm's quarter-scale R&D acceleration.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


_QUARTER_BARS = 63


def _quarter_change_rank(value: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cross-sectionally normalize a causal quarter-scale fundamental change."""
    change = value - value.shift(_QUARTER_BARS)
    return change.rank(axis=1, pct=True)


def _realization_rank(
    gross_profit_growth: pd.DataFrame,
    operating_margin: pd.DataFrame,
    operating_cash_flow_growth: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Reward synchronized, rather than one-off, productivity improvement."""
    gross = _quarter_change_rank(gross_profit_growth)
    margin = _quarter_change_rank(operating_margin)
    cash = _quarter_change_rank(operating_cash_flow_growth)

    average = (gross + margin + cash) / 3.0
    disagreement = np.sqrt(
        ((gross - average) ** 2 + (margin - average) ** 2 + (cash - average) ** 2)
        / 3.0
    )
    return (average - 0.5 * disagreement).rank(axis=1, pct=True)


@register_factor
class RdConditionedIntangibleRealization(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "rd_conditioned_intangible_realization"
    name = "R&D-Conditioned Intangible Realization"
    category = "other"
    description = (
        "Scales coherent intangible-productivity realization by quarter-scale "
        "R&D acceleration, emphasizing intangible-heavy firms where rising "
        "research investment is supported by improving operating economics."
    )
    window_length = 63
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "intangiblesToAssets",
        "rdToRevenue",
        "rdExpenseGrowth",
        "grossProfitGrowth",
        "operatingMargin",
        "operatingCashFlowGrowth",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        intangible = data["intangiblesToAssets"].reindex_like(close)
        rd_intensity = data["rdToRevenue"].reindex_like(close)
        rd_growth = data["rdExpenseGrowth"].reindex_like(close)
        gross_growth = data["grossProfitGrowth"].reindex_like(close)
        operating_margin = data["operatingMargin"].reindex_like(close)
        cash_growth = data["operatingCashFlowGrowth"].reindex_like(close)

        intangible_rank = intangible.rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        rd_state = (
            _quarter_change_rank(rd_intensity)
            + _quarter_change_rank(rd_growth)
        ) / 2.0
        realization = _realization_rank(gross_growth, operating_margin, cash_growth)

        valid = (
            intangible.notna()
            & rd_intensity.notna()
            & rd_growth.notna()
            & gross_growth.notna()
            & operating_margin.notna()
            & cash_growth.notna()
            & rd_state.notna()
            & realization.notna()
        )

        raw = intangible_rank * rd_state * (realization - 0.5)
        return raw.where(valid).rank(axis=1, pct=True).reindex_like(close).fillna(0.5)
programs.name: R&D-Conditioned Intangible Realization
programs.trading_idea: R&D scaling is primarily a state variable: additional research spending is valuable when an intangible-heavy firm is demonstrably converting investment into synchronized gross-profit, operating-margin, and cash-flow improvement. The child therefore conditions Parent A's productivity-realization signal on Parent B's R&D-acceleration state, rather than rewarding either high intangibles or high R&D spend in isolation. This interaction identifies firms where the market may still expense a growing research program while operational evidence shows that the intangible asset base is beginning to monetize; the converse identifies research spenders whose weak realization makes the investment less credible.
programs.description: Ranks intangible-intensive firms by a coherent quarter-scale improvement in gross-profit growth, operating margin, and operating-cash-flow growth, with the exposure scaled by cross-sectional R&D intensity and R&D-expense-growth acceleration. High R&D acceleration amplifies productive realization and penalizes deteriorating realization, while low-R&D names remain comparatively neutral.

"""Closing-inventory schedule completion.

Repeated abnormal-volume closes at a directional extreme can reflect benchmarked
or closing-auction execution rather than durable information.  Once a coherent
multi-bar inventory schedule is completed, the temporary price concession is
expected to unwind over the following week.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _closing_schedule_pressure(
    open_: pd.DataFrame,
    high: pd.DataFrame,
    low: pd.DataFrame,
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal estimate of coherent temporary closing-auction pressure."""
    bar_range = (high - low).clip(lower=0.0)
    safe_range = bar_range.replace(0.0, np.nan)

    close_location = ((2.0 * close - high - low) / safe_range).clip(-1.0, 1.0)
    body_direction = np.sign(close - open_)
    efficiency = ((close - open_).abs() / safe_range).clip(0.0, 1.0)

    # The baseline excludes today's volume, preventing the event from partly
    # normalising itself while retaining a strictly trailing construction.
    volume_base = volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=10).median()
    relative_volume = (volume / volume_base.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(0.0, 6.0)
    abnormality = np.log1p(relative_volume)

    daily_pressure = (
        close_location.fillna(0.0)
        * body_direction.fillna(0.0)
        * efficiency.fillna(0.0)
        * abnormality.fillna(0.0)
    )

    signed_sum = daily_pressure.rolling(4, min_periods=3).sum()
    absolute_sum = daily_pressure.abs().rolling(4, min_periods=3).sum()
    coherence = (signed_sum.abs() / absolute_sum.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(0.0, 1.0)

    # Reverse coherent cumulative pressure: persistent buying/selling from a
    # closing execution schedule is expected to relax after completion.
    return (-signed_sum * coherence).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


@register_factor
class ClosingInventoryScheduleCompletion(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "closing_inventory_schedule_completion"
    name = "Closing Inventory Schedule Completion"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Cross-sectional rank of the reversal of coherent four-bar "
        "abnormal-volume directional closing pressure, targeting temporary "
        "closing-auction inventory schedules rather than isolated bar moves."
    )
    window_length = 24
    inputs = ["open", "high", "low", "close", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        open_ = data["open"]
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"].clip(lower=0.0)

        signal = _closing_schedule_pressure(open_, high, low, close, volume)
        return rank(signal).fillna(0.5)
programs.name: Closing Inventory Schedule Completion
programs.trading_idea: The parent report indicates that efficient, abnormal-volume closes near an extreme are not information-driven continuation signals on average; they are more consistent with temporary closing-auction inventory pressure. This child identifies repeated, directionally coherent pressure across several bars, treating it as a benchmarked execution schedule whose completion leaves a short-lived price concession that mean-reverts over the next week. The edge should persist because index, fund-flow, and end-of-day execution demand is mechanically inelastic in timing, while daily-bar observers cannot directly identify the underlying participant or distinguish a completion from a genuinely informed repricing. It is falsified if multi-day coherent closing pressure continues to predict same-direction returns after reversing its sign.
programs.description: Computes abnormal-volume, range-efficient directional closing pressure, aggregates it over four trailing bars, and increases its weight when the pressure has a coherent sign. The factor longs names with persistent sell-side closing pressure and shorts names with persistent buy-side closing pressure.

"""Delayed repricing of innovations in filing-level cash earnings quality."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _prior_filing_value(value: pd.DataFrame, update: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return the value observed at the preceding detected filing update.

    The event-only series is forward-filled and shifted by one bar, so an
    update at t is compared only with information available before t.
    """
    return value.where(update).ffill().shift(1)


@register_factor
class FilingCashQualityInnovationLag(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "filing_cash_quality_innovation_lag"
    name = "Filing Cash-Quality Innovation Lag"
    category = "other"
    description = (
        "Ranks profitable firms by the filing-to-filing improvement in income "
        "quality, carrying each fresh filing innovation for six bars."
    )
    window_length = 6
    inputs = ["close", "incomeQuality", "netIncome"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        template = data["close"]
        quality = data["incomeQuality"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        net_income = data["netIncome"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        previous_income = net_income.shift(1)
        update = (
            net_income.notna()
            & previous_income.notna()
            & net_income.ne(previous_income)
        )

        prior_quality = _prior_filing_value(quality, update)
        prior_net_income = _prior_filing_value(net_income, update)
        innovation = quality - prior_quality

        valid = (
            update
            & net_income.gt(0.0)
            & prior_net_income.gt(0.0)
            & quality.notna()
            & prior_quality.notna()
        )

        event_signal = innovation.where(valid)
        event_signal = event_signal.mask(update & ~valid, 0.0)
        held_signal = event_signal.ffill(limit=5)

        return rank(held_signal).reindex_like(template).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Filing Cash-Quality Innovation Lag
programs.trading_idea: Investors often react first to the headline earnings level at a filing, while the change in the degree to which earnings convert into operating cash is incorporated more slowly. A positive filing-to-filing innovation in income quality indicates that reported profitability has become more cash-backed and should receive a delayed repricing over the following week. The effect should persist because detailed cash-flow reconciliation is costly to process immediately, but it is falsified if positive cash-quality innovations do not predict stronger six-bar returns after controlling for the report-date cross-section.
programs.description: At each detected net-income filing update, the factor measures the change from the prior filing in operating-cash-flow-to-net-income quality for profitable firms. The innovation is held for six calendar bars and ranked cross-sectionally.

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _rolling_impact_slope(close: pd.DataFrame, volume: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    safe_close = close.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    ret = safe_close.pct_change().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    log_volume = np.log(volume.where(volume > 0.0))
    vol_mean = log_volume.rolling(30, min_periods=15).mean()
    vol_std = log_volume.rolling(30, min_periods=15).std()
    z_volume = (log_volume - vol_mean) / vol_std.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    covariance = z_volume.rolling(15, min_periods=8).cov(ret)
    variance = z_volume.rolling(15, min_periods=8).var()
    return covariance / variance.replace(0.0, np.nan)


def _close_location(high: pd.DataFrame, low: pd.DataFrame, close: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    bar_range = (high - low).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    location = (2.0 * close - high - low) / bar_range
    return location.clip(lower=-1.0, upper=1.0).fillna(0.0)


def _fundamental_novelty_gate(
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    eps_surprise: pd.DataFrame,
    revenue_surprise: pd.DataFrame,
    revenue_estimate: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    safe_price = close.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    safe_estimate = revenue_estimate.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)

    eps_change = eps_surprise.diff().abs() / safe_price
    revenue_change = revenue_surprise.diff().abs() / safe_estimate

    novelty = eps_change.fillna(0.0) + revenue_change.fillna(0.0)
    novelty = novelty.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)

    return 1.0 / (1.0 + 12.0 * novelty.clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0))


@register_factor
class FundamentalVetoedImpactBreakReversal(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = 'fundamental_vetoed_impact_break_reversal'
    name = 'Fundamental-Vetoed Impact Reversal'
    category = 'microstructure'
    description = (
        'Fades close-location-signed return-volume impact breaks, but downweights '
        'observations coinciding with fresh EPS or revenue-surprise information.'
    )
    window_length = 110
    inputs = ['close', 'high', 'low', 'volume', 'epsSurprise', 'revenueSurprise', 'revenueEstimate']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        slope = _rolling_impact_slope(data['close'], data['volume'])
        historical_mean = slope.shift(1).rolling(80, min_periods=40).mean()
        historical_std = slope.shift(1).rolling(80, min_periods=40).std()
        slope_break = (slope - historical_mean) / historical_std.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        positive_break = slope_break.clip(lower=0.0, upper=6.0).fillna(0.0)
        rejection = _close_location(data['high'], data['low'], data['close'])
        information_gate = _fundamental_novelty_gate(
            data['close'],
            data['epsSurprise'],
            data['revenueSurprise'],
            data['revenueEstimate'],
        )

        signal = -positive_break * rejection * information_gate
        return rank(signal).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.5)
programs.name: Fundamental-Vetoed Impact Reversal
programs.trading_idea: Temporary execution pressure can create a return-volume impact break and an intrabar rejection, but the same pattern around a fresh earnings or revenue surprise is more likely informed price discovery than inventory exhaustion. The child therefore preserves the parent's impact-break reversal mechanism only when contemporaneous fundamental-surprise novelty is low. This is falsifiable: impact-break reversals should be materially stronger in the low-novelty subset, while high-novelty observations should exhibit weaker reversal or continuation; the edge persists because liquidity-driven execution and the interpretation of new accounting information are costly to distinguish in real time.
programs.description: Computes the parent's abnormal return-volume slope break, fades its close-location direction, and attenuates the reversal signal when EPS or revenue surprises have just changed materially relative to price or estimated revenue.

"""Fresh replacement-capex deficits that receive headline applause can reverse.

Mechanism: A newly reported capex-to-depreciation shortfall may be rewarded as
near-term free-cash-flow improvement even though it implies deferred asset renewal.
The signal isolates those fresh disclosures with unusually positive immediate price
reactions, where the capacity-risk interpretation is likely underweighted initially.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

def _fresh_report_window(values: pd.DataFrame, bars: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal indicator for the bars immediately following a real report update."""
    prior = values.shift(1)
    updated = values.notna() & prior.notna() & values.ne(prior)
    return updated.astype(float).rolling(bars, min_periods=1).max()

@register_factor
class RenewalDeficitReportReactionGap(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = 'renewal_deficit_report_reaction_gap_j'
    name = 'Renewal Deficit Reaction Gap'
    category = 'other'
    description = 'Fresh capex-to-depreciation replacement deficits interacted with a positive immediate price reaction; high scores are expected to underperform as deferred renewal risk is reassessed.'
    window_length = 6
    inputs = ['capex', 'depreciationAmortization', 'close']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        capex = data['capex']
        depreciation = data['depreciationAmortization']
        close = data['close']
        depreciation_base = depreciation.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        replacement_ratio = (capex.abs() / depreciation_base).clip(0.0, 4.0)
        replacement_deficit = (1.0 - replacement_ratio).clip(-2.0, 1.0)
        ratio_available = replacement_ratio.where(capex.notna() & depreciation_base.notna())
        fresh = _fresh_report_window(ratio_available, 5).astype(bool)
        daily_return = close.pct_change()
        two_day_return = daily_return.rolling(3, min_periods=2).sum()
        cross_sectional_reaction = two_day_return.sub(two_day_return.median(axis=1), axis=0)
        deficit_score = rank(replacement_deficit)
        applause_score = rank(cross_sectional_reaction)
        event_score = 0.65 * deficit_score + 0.35 * applause_score
        valid = fresh & replacement_deficit.notna() & cross_sectional_reaction.notna()
        return rank(event_score.where(valid)).fillna(0.5)
programs.name: Renewal Deficit Reaction Gap (jitter)
programs.trading_idea: A newly disclosed capex-to-depreciation shortfall is most informative at the reporting event, rather than as a stale quarterly level: investors can initially reward the apparent cash-flow improvement while underweighting the implied replacement-capacity risk. The child shorts firms with the largest fresh replacement deficit that nevertheless receive an unusually positive two-day price reaction, a direct measure of headline-cash-flow applause. The edge should persist for roughly a week because fundamental-capacity implications require slower analyst and investor reassessment than the initial earnings reaction; it is falsified if these positively received renewal deficits do not subsequently underperform comparable fresh disclosures.
programs.description: Ranks fresh capex-versus-depreciation deficits only during the five bars after a fundamental update, interacting them with an above-cross-sectional-median two-day price response. High values identify firms whose apparent cash-flow benefit was positively received despite a newly disclosed replacement-investment gap.

programs.code:
"""Cash-validated repair after adverse effective-tax-rate disclosures.

Mechanism: a booked tax-rate increase can produce a headline-negative earnings
interpretation even when contemporaneous operating-cash realization improves.
A negative initial price reaction to this cash-validated event is more likely to
be a transitory accounting interpretation than a persistent cash-flow loss.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, returns
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _report_change_and_age(series: pd.DataFrame) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Return the latest disclosed change and bars since that disclosure.

    Quarterly point-in-time fields are step functions.  A change is recorded
    only when the observed value changes from the preceding available bar, and
    both the change and its event age are then carried forward causally.
    """
    previous = series.shift(1)
    event = series.notna() & (previous.isna() | series.ne(previous))
    prior_report = series.where(event).ffill().shift(1)
    change = (series - prior_report).where(event & prior_report.notna()).ffill()

    counter_values = np.broadcast_to(
        np.arange(len(series), dtype=float)[:, None], series.shape
    ).copy()
    counter = pd.DataFrame(counter_values, index=series.index, columns=series.columns)
    latest_event = counter.where(event).ffill()
    age = counter - latest_event
    return change, age


@register_factor
class TaxDisclosureReactionCashValidation(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "tax_disclosure_reaction_cash_validation"
    name = "Tax Disclosure Cash-Validation Repair"
    category = "mean_reversion"
    description = (
        "Fresh effective-tax-rate increases confirmed by improving operating-cash "
        "realization and followed by a negative, volatility-scaled price reaction."
    )
    window_length = 60
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "incomeTaxExpense",
        "incomeBeforeTax",
        "operatingCashFlow",
        "netIncome",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        pretax = data["incomeBeforeTax"]
        tax_expense = data["incomeTaxExpense"]
        net_income = data["netIncome"]
        operating_cash_flow = data["operatingCashFlow"]

        positive_pretax = pretax.where(pretax > 0.0)
        tax_rate = (tax_expense / positive_pretax).clip(-0.50, 1.50)
        tax_change, tax_age = _report_change_and_age(tax_rate)

        positive_income = net_income.where(net_income > 0.0)
        cash_realization = (operating_cash_flow / positive_income).clip(-5.0, 5.0)
        cash_change, _ = _report_change_and_age(cash_realization)

        ret = returns(data)
        three_bar_return = close / close.shift(3) - 1.0
        trailing_vol = ret.rolling(60, min_periods=20).std()
        adverse_reaction = -three_bar_return / trailing_vol.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        # High tax-rate and cash-realization changes jointly identify the
        # accounting-versus-cash discrepancy.  The reaction leg selects cases
        # where the market has actually priced the headline tax item negatively.
        fundamental_confirmation = rank(tax_change) + rank(cash_change) - 1.0
        reaction_confirmation = rank(adverse_reaction) - 0.5
        raw_score = fundamental_confirmation + 0.75 * reaction_confirmation

        # A filing interpretation is a temporary event; decay it rather than
        # allowing a quarterly observation to become a static style exposure.
        freshness = np.exp(-tax_age.clip(lower=0.0) / 7.0)
        recent = tax_age.le(15.0)
        eligible = (
            positive_pretax.notna()
            & positive_income.notna()
            & tax_change.notna()
            & cash_change.notna()
            & adverse_reaction.notna()
            & recent
        )
        return (raw_score * freshness).where(eligible, 0.0).reindex_like(close).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Tax Disclosure Cash-Validation Repair
programs.trading_idea: A sharp increase in the reported effective tax rate is often treated as bad earnings news, but its informational content is weaker when the same filing shows an improvement in operating-cash realization. The child isolates these recent disclosure events and buys firms with a tax-rate shock, improving cash conversion, and an initially negative price reaction, where investors appear to have extrapolated a booked-tax item into a persistent cash-flow impairment. The edge should persist because interpreting discrete tax accounting items requires joint reading of the tax and cash-flow statements, while immediate trading attention is concentrated on headline earnings; it is falsified if these cash-validated tax shocks do not subsequently outperform after the initial adverse reaction.
programs.description: Ranks recent effective-tax-rate increases jointly with changes in operating-cash-flow realization, then emphasizes names whose filing-period price response was negative relative to their own recent volatility. The score decays after 15 bars so it represents a fresh disclosure-repair signal rather than a persistent value or quality exposure.

"""Capacity quality from replacement investment and productive-asset utilization.

Mechanism: underinvestment relative to depreciation is most adverse when the
existing asset base is also becoming less productive.  The joint condition is a
broader capacity-quality signal than an event-reaction fade: firms that defer
replacement while asset turnover falls face a gradually recognized deterioration
in operating capacity and should underperform.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _quarterly_utilization_change(turnover: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal approximately-quarterly percentage change in asset turnover."""
    prior = turnover.shift(63)
    denominator = prior.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return ((turnover - prior) / denominator).clip(-2.0, 2.0)


@register_factor
class RenewalUtilizationCapacityQuality(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "renewal_utilization_capacity_quality"
    name = "Renewal-Utilization Capacity Quality"
    category = "other"
    description = (
        "Inverse joint rank of replacement-capex deficit and deteriorating "
        "quarterly asset turnover; high scores identify stronger capacity quality."
    )
    window_length = 63
    inputs = ["close", "capex", "depreciationAmortization", "assetTurnover"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        capex = data["capex"]
        depreciation = data["depreciationAmortization"]
        turnover = data["assetTurnover"]

        depreciation_base = depreciation.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        replacement_ratio = (capex.abs() / depreciation_base).clip(0.0, 4.0)
        replacement_deficit = (1.0 - replacement_ratio).clip(-1.0, 1.0)

        turnover_change = _quarterly_utilization_change(turnover)
        utilization_deterioration = (-turnover_change).clip(-2.0, 2.0)

        valid = (
            replacement_deficit.notna()
            & utilization_deterioration.notna()
            & np.isfinite(replacement_deficit)
            & np.isfinite(utilization_deterioration)
        )
        deficit_rank = rank(replacement_deficit.where(valid))
        deterioration_rank = rank(utilization_deterioration.where(valid))
        capacity_risk = deficit_rank * deterioration_rank

        signal = rank((-capacity_risk).where(valid))
        return signal.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).fillna(0.5)
programs.name: Renewal-Utilization Capacity Quality
programs.trading_idea: A capex shortfall is economically harmful primarily when a firm's existing asset base is already becoming less productive, rather than whenever capex is below depreciation. Firms simultaneously underinvesting in replacement capacity and experiencing falling asset turnover should underperform over the next six trading days as investors and analysts incorporate the joint evidence of deteriorating operating capacity. The effect should persist because evaluating replacement investment together with utilization requires reconciling several accounting-line items and is less salient than headline earnings or free cash flow; it is falsified if the lowest-score renewal-and-utilization cohort does not underperform after controlling for the individual signals.
programs.description: Ranks firms by the inverse of a joint capacity-risk score: replacement-capex deficit multiplied by quarter-over-quarter deterioration in asset turnover. High values identify firms with adequately renewed, stable-or-improving productive asset bases.

programs.code:
"""Failed optimistic auctions conditional on acquisition and working-capital fragility.

Mechanism: a positive opening gap that is sold through the session is more
informative when a firm recently expanded goodwill while its cash conversion
cycle deteriorated.  This combines a slow accounting credibility state with a
fast revealed-demand test at the opening auction.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _quarterly_change_zscore(
    frame: pd.DataFrame, lag: int, window: int, minimum: int
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal robustly clipped z-score of a positive-lag fundamental change."""
    clean = frame.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    change = clean - clean.shift(lag)
    mean = change.rolling(window, min_periods=minimum).mean()
    scale = change.rolling(window, min_periods=minimum).std()
    return ((change - mean) / scale.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(-4.0, 4.0)


@register_factor
class AcquisitionCreditAuctionCredibilityBreak(BaseFactor):
    """Short fragile acquisitive firms whose optimistic opening gap is rejected."""

    factor_id = "acquisition_credit_auction_credibility_break"
    name = "Acquisition Credit Auction Credibility Break"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Negative rank of high-volume positive opening gaps that reverse intrabar, "
        "conditioned on abnormal goodwill buildup and worsening cash conversion."
    )
    window_length = 252
    inputs = [
        "open",
        "close",
        "volume",
        "goodwill",
        "investedCapital",
        "cashConversionCycle",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        open_ = data["open"]
        volume = data["volume"]

        lag = 63
        capital = data["investedCapital"].abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        prior_capital = capital.shift(lag).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        goodwill_build = (
            (data["goodwill"] - data["goodwill"].shift(lag)) / prior_capital
        )
        acquisition_pressure = _quarterly_change_zscore(
            goodwill_build, lag, 252, 126
        ).clip(lower=0.0)
        credit_deterioration = (-_quarterly_change_zscore(
            -data["cashConversionCycle"], lag, 252, 126
        )).clip(lower=0.0)
        fragility = np.sqrt(acquisition_pressure * credit_deterioration)

        safe_open = open_.where(open_ > 0.0)
        safe_close = close.where(close > 0.0)
        gap = np.log(safe_open / safe_close.shift(1))
        intrabar = np.log(safe_close / safe_open)

        gap_scale = gap.rolling(60, min_periods=20).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        body_scale = intrabar.rolling(20, min_periods=10).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        positive_gap = (gap / gap_scale).clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0)
        rejection = (-intrabar / body_scale).clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0)

        clean_volume = volume.where(volume > 0.0)
        volume_base = clean_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=10).mean().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        participation = np.sqrt((clean_volume / volume_base).clip(lower=0.0, upper=4.0))

        auction_failure = positive_gap * rejection * participation
        stress = fragility * auction_failure
        valid = fragility.notna() & auction_failure.notna()
        signal = rank((-stress).where(valid))

        return (
            signal.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
            .replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
            .fillna(0.5)
            - 0.5
        )
programs.name: Acquisition Credit Auction Credibility Break
programs.trading_idea: Acquisition-driven balance-sheet expansion accompanied by worsening cash-conversion-cycle dynamics identifies firms whose reported operating progress is vulnerable to financing or integration scrutiny. A positive opening repricing that is then sold down through the session on unusually high participation is a timely revealed-preference signal that liquidity providers and investors do not validate that optimistic valuation. The interaction has edge because accounting fragility alone is slow-moving and gap rejection alone is often noise, whereas a failed optimistic auction in a fragile post-acquisition state identifies a near-term credibility unwind.
programs.description: Builds a quarterly-state fragility gate from abnormal goodwill accumulation and deteriorating cash conversion, then applies it only to positive overnight gaps that reverse intrabar on elevated volume. The factor is negative for the largest fragile-state auction failures and neutral when fundamental coverage is unavailable.

programs.code:
"""Fresh sales-collection mismatch after a revenue report.

Mechanism: a headline revenue beat is less durable when receivables grow faster
than sales, indicating that reported sales may not translate into cash.  The
signal is active only at a fresh report, when headline-focused investors can
initially underweight the collection-quality warning.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _fresh_update(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal indicator for a new non-missing PIT report observation."""
    clean = frame.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    prior = clean.shift(1)
    return (clean.notna() & (prior.isna() | clean.ne(prior))).astype(float)


@register_factor
class FreshSalesCollectionMismatch(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "fresh_sales_collection_mismatch"
    name = "Fresh Sales-Collection Mismatch"
    category = "other"
    description = (
        "At fresh revenue reports, shorts positive sales surprises whose "
        "receivables growth exceeds reported revenue growth; zero otherwise."
    )
    window_length = 2
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "revenueActual",
        "revenueEstimate",
        "receivablesGrowth",
        "revenueGrowth",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        template = data["close"]
        actual = data["revenueActual"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        estimate = data["revenueEstimate"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        receivables_growth = data["receivablesGrowth"].replace(
            [np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan
        )
        revenue_growth = data["revenueGrowth"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        surprise = (actual - estimate) / estimate.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        collection_mismatch = receivables_growth - revenue_growth
        fresh = _fresh_update(actual)

        valid = surprise.notna() & collection_mismatch.notna() & fresh.eq(1.0)
        # A high positive surprise coupled with weak collection quality is adverse.
        signal = -(rank(surprise) - 0.5) * (rank(collection_mismatch) - 0.5)
        return signal.where(valid, 0.0).fillna(0.0).reindex_like(template)
programs.name: Fresh Sales-Collection Mismatch
programs.trading_idea: A positive revenue surprise is less credible when receivables are simultaneously growing faster than sales: reported demand may have been supported by looser customer credit rather than cash-realized end demand. The child therefore targets the short post-report window in which investors initially extrapolate the headline sales beat before processing the balance-sheet implication. The edge should persist because receivable quality is heterogeneous across firms and requires combining multiple filing fields, while fast traders tend to react first to the salient revenue surprise rather than the slower-to-interpret collection mismatch.
programs.description: On fresh revenue-report updates, the signal shorts firms with a large positive revenue surprise and unusually high receivables growth relative to revenue growth. It is zero outside fresh reporting events, concentrating the state variable in the six-bar post-disclosure assimilation window.

programs.code:
"""Collection deterioration conditional on an uncovered refinancing wall.

Mechanism: delayed collections are most adverse when cash and operating cash
flow cannot cover near-term debt.  The interaction identifies trade-credit
stress that immediately reduces the resources available for refinancing.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _carried_report_change(values: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Latest observed report-to-report change of a PIT step series.

    The result is causal: a change is recognized only on its availability bar
    and is then carried until the next observed update or a data-staleness gap.
    """
    clean = values.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    prior = clean.shift(1)
    changed = clean.notna() & prior.notna() & clean.ne(prior)
    return (clean - prior).where(changed).ffill().where(clean.notna())


def _refinancing_capacity_risk(
    short_term_debt: pd.DataFrame,
    total_debt: pd.DataFrame,
    cash: pd.DataFrame,
    operating_cash_flow: pd.DataFrame,
    interest_coverage: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Near-term debt burden not funded by internally available liquidity."""
    short_debt = short_term_debt.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(lower=0.0)
    debt = total_debt.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    cash_clean = cash.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(lower=0.0)
    ocf = operating_cash_flow.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(lower=0.0)

    maturity_share = short_debt / debt.where(debt > 0.0)
    liquidity_deficit = (short_debt - cash_clean - ocf).clip(lower=0.0)
    liquidity_deficit = liquidity_deficit / short_debt.where(short_debt > 0.0)

    coverage = interest_coverage.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    coverage_burden = 1.0 / (1.0 + coverage.clip(lower=0.0))
    coverage_burden = coverage_burden.fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)

    return maturity_share * liquidity_deficit * (1.0 + coverage_burden)


@register_factor
class CollectionTrappedRefinancingCliff(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "collection_trapped_refinancing_cliff"
    name = "Collection-Trapped Refinancing Cliff"
    category = "carry"
    description = (
        "Inverse rank of receivable-collection deterioration gated by an "
        "uncovered short-term refinancing requirement."
    )
    window_length = 63
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "daysSalesOutstanding",
        "daysPayablesOutstanding",
        "shortTermDebt",
        "totalDebt",
        "cash",
        "operatingCashFlow",
        "interestCoverage",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        template = data["close"]
        dso = data["daysSalesOutstanding"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        dpo = data["daysPayablesOutstanding"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        collection_gap = dso - dpo
        collection_deterioration = _carried_report_change(collection_gap)
        positive_collection_stress = collection_deterioration.where(
            collection_deterioration > 0.0
        )

        refinancing_risk = _refinancing_capacity_risk(
            data["shortTermDebt"],
            data["totalDebt"],
            data["cash"],
            data["operatingCashFlow"],
            data["interestCoverage"],
        )

        valid = (
            dso.notna()
            & dpo.notna()
            & data["shortTermDebt"].notna()
            & data["totalDebt"].notna()
            & data["cash"].notna()
            & data["operatingCashFlow"].notna()
            & refinancing_risk.notna()
            & collection_deterioration.notna()
        )

        adverse_state = rank(refinancing_risk) * rank(positive_collection_stress)
        defensive_signal = -rank(adverse_state)
        return defensive_signal.where(valid & adverse_state.notna(), 0.5).fillna(0.5).reindex_like(template)
programs.name: Collection-Trapped Refinancing Cliff
programs.trading_idea: A widening receivable-versus-payable-days gap is economically dangerous only when short-dated debt cannot be covered by cash and operating cash flow. In that constrained state, delayed customer collections directly reduce the internal liquidity available for an approaching maturity wall, creating a sharper equity repricing risk than either weak refinancing capacity or working-capital deterioration alone. The interaction isolates firms where trade-credit extension changes from a commercial-policy detail into an immediate funding shortfall, so the factor is defensive: high values indicate low combined stress and should precede relatively higher returns.
programs.description: Computes a carried-forward report-to-report deterioration in the receivable-minus-payable-days spread and gates it by a refinancing-capacity deficit based on short-term debt, cash, operating cash flow, and interest coverage. The returned signal is the inverse cross-sectional rank of the adverse interaction, with neutral values when the required balance-sheet or working-capital fields are unavailable.

programs.code:
"""Firms with a large short-term-debt share are vulnerable when cash generation and liquid balances do not cover the approaching refinancing need. This risk is often only gradually incorporated after quarterly statements because equity investors focus on earnings while creditors and treasury desks react more quickly to debt-service capacity. The effect should disappear for firms whose operating cash flow, cash balance, and interest coverage are sufficient to refinance internally."""
from __future__ import annotations
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

def _refinancing_risk(short_term_debt: pd.DataFrame, total_debt: pd.DataFrame, cash: pd.DataFrame, operating_cash_flow: pd.DataFrame, interest_coverage: pd.DataFrame, interest_expense: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Build a causal balance-sheet refinancing-risk score from PIT fields."""
    short_term_debt = short_term_debt.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    total_debt = total_debt.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    cash = cash.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    operating_cash_flow = operating_cash_flow.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    debt_base = total_debt.where(total_debt > 0.0)
    maturity_share = short_term_debt.clip(lower=0.0) / debt_base
    internal_liquidity = cash.clip(lower=0.0) + operating_cash_flow.clip(lower=0.0)
    capacity_deficit = (short_term_debt.clip(lower=0.0) - internal_liquidity).clip(lower=0.0) / short_term_debt.where(short_term_debt > 0.0)
    coverage = interest_coverage.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    coverage_weakness = 1.0 / (1.0 + coverage.clip(lower=0.0))
    coverage_weakness = coverage_weakness.fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
    current_interest = interest_expense.abs().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    prior_interest = current_interest.shift(60)
    interest_increase = (current_interest - prior_interest).clip(lower=0.0) / (current_interest + prior_interest).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    interest_increase = interest_increase.fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
    return maturity_share * capacity_deficit * (1.0 + coverage_weakness) * (1.0 + interest_increase)

@register_factor
class MaturityWallCashflowGap(BaseFactor):
    """Negative rank of short-dated refinancing need unsupported by liquidity."""
    factor_id = 'maturity_wall_cashflow_gap_j'
    name = 'Near-Term Refinancing Capacity Gap'
    category = 'other'
    description = 'Negative cross-sectional rank of short-term debt exposure times the cash-and-operating-cash-flow refinancing deficit, with extra weight for weak interest coverage and rising interest expense.'
    window_length = 63
    inputs = ['shortTermDebt', 'totalDebt', 'cash', 'operatingCashFlow', 'interestCoverage', 'interestExpense']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        risk = _refinancing_risk(data['shortTermDebt'], data['totalDebt'], data['cash'], data['operatingCashFlow'], data['interestCoverage'], data['interestExpense'])
        return (-rank(risk)).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Near-Term Refinancing Capacity Gap (jitter)
programs.trading_idea: Firms with a large short-term-debt share are vulnerable when cash generation and liquid balances do not cover the approaching refinancing need. This risk is often only gradually incorporated after quarterly statements because equity investors focus on earnings while creditors and treasury desks react more quickly to debt-service capacity. The effect should disappear for firms whose operating cash flow, cash balance, and interest coverage are sufficient to refinance internally.
programs.description: Rank firms negatively by shortTermDebt relative to totalDebt, scaled by the deficit between shortTermDebt and cash plus operatingCashFlow, with additional weight on weak interestCoverage and rising interestExpense.

programs.code:
"""Headline revenue beats with worsening collection quality.

Mechanism: investors initially react to a positive reported revenue surprise, but a
simultaneous increase in receivables relative to revenue can reveal that sales
were supported by weaker cash collection. Balance-sheet detail is less salient
than the headline beat, so the resulting reassessment can occur over the next
several trading days.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _fresh_report_change(
    ratio: pd.DataFrame, surprise: pd.DataFrame, persistence: int
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Return a causal, briefly carried report-time ratio innovation.

    Fundamental fields are point-in-time quarterly step functions. A change in
    revenue surprise marks a newly available report; the contemporaneous change
    in the receivables-to-revenue ratio is then carried only through the short
    post-disclosure attention window.
    """
    prior_surprise = surprise.shift(1)
    report_event = (
        surprise.notna()
        & prior_surprise.notna()
        & surprise.ne(prior_surprise)
    )
    ratio_change = (ratio - ratio.shift(1)).where(report_event)
    fresh_change = ratio_change.ffill(limit=persistence - 1)
    fresh_event = report_event.astype(float).replace(0.0, np.nan).ffill(
        limit=persistence - 1
    ).notna()
    return fresh_change, fresh_event


@register_factor
class HeadlineBeatCollectionFade(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "headline_beat_collection_quality_fade"
    name = "Headline Beat Collection Fade"
    category = "other"
    description = (
        "Shorts fresh positive revenue-surprise disclosures where receivables "
        "rise relative to revenue, indicating that headline sales strength may "
        "be supported by deteriorating collection quality."
    )
    window_length = 6
    inputs = ["close", "receivables", "revenue", "revenueSurprise"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        template = data["close"]
        receivables = data["receivables"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        revenue = data["revenue"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        surprise = data["revenueSurprise"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        collection_intensity = receivables / revenue.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        intensity_change, fresh_report = _fresh_report_change(
            collection_intensity, surprise, 6
        )

        # Only a positive headline beat with worsening receivable intensity is
        # adverse. Cross-sectional ranks avoid comparing raw accounting scales.
        positive_beat = surprise.where(surprise > 0.0)
        worsening_collection = intensity_change.where(intensity_change > 0.0)
        adverse_signal = rank(worsening_collection) * rank(positive_beat)

        valid = (
            fresh_report
            & worsening_collection.notna()
            & positive_beat.notna()
        )
        return rank(adverse_signal).where(valid, 0.0).fillna(0.0).reindex_like(template)
programs.name: Headline Beat Collection Fade
programs.trading_idea: A positive revenue surprise is initially salient, but its quality is weaker when receivables rise faster than reported sales at the same disclosure. This identifies firms whose headline beat may reflect looser customer credit or delayed collection rather than durable demand, producing a negative reassessment during the following week as investors process the balance-sheet detail. The effect should persist because headline revenue surprises receive more immediate attention than changes in collection intensity, while accounting timing and firm-specific payment terms make the signal costly to arbitrage mechanically.
programs.description: Ranks fresh reporting events with both a positive revenue surprise and an increase in receivables as a share of revenue. The adverse collection change is retained for six bars after the disclosure to target the near-term post-report processing window.

programs.code:
"""Fade gap retention when a firm's working-capital funding structure is fragile.

Mechanism: intrabar confirmation of an overnight repricing is normally ambiguous,
but is more likely to be temporary inventory transfer when a firm faces a worsening
short-duration funding requirement against slow cash conversion.  The factor only
expresses the gap-fade signal in that balance-sheet state.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _neutral_rank(values: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    clean = values.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    return rank(clean).fillna(0.5)


def _funding_fragility(
    short_debt: pd.DataFrame,
    total_debt: pd.DataFrame,
    cash_cycle: pd.DataFrame,
    current_ratio: pd.DataFrame,
    ocf_growth: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cross-sectional funding stress using only available point-in-time data."""
    total = total_debt.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).where(lambda x: x > 0.0)
    short_share = short_debt.clip(lower=0.0) / total

    # Sixty-three daily bars approximates one reporting quarter.  These changes
    # are causal and remain stable between point-in-time fundamental updates.
    cycle_worsening = cash_cycle - cash_cycle.shift(63)
    liquidity_worsening = -(current_ratio - current_ratio.shift(63))
    cashflow_weakness = (-ocf_growth).clip(lower=0.0)

    state = (
        0.40 * _neutral_rank(short_share)
        + 0.25 * _neutral_rank(cycle_worsening)
        + 0.20 * _neutral_rank(liquidity_worsening)
        + 0.15 * _neutral_rank(cashflow_weakness)
    )

    # Do not manufacture a state before the debt structure is observable.
    return state.where(short_share.notna())


def _gap_retention(
    open_: pd.DataFrame,
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Signed strength of overnight information retained by the daytime auction."""
    safe_open = open_.where(open_ > 0.0)
    safe_close = close.where(close > 0.0)
    prior_close = safe_close.shift(1)

    gap = np.log(safe_open / prior_close)
    intrabar = np.log(safe_close / safe_open)
    gap = gap.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    intrabar = intrabar.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

    gap_scale = gap.rolling(60, min_periods=20).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    gap_z = (gap.abs() / gap_scale).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    gap_gate = (gap_z / (1.0 + gap_z)).fillna(0.0)

    intrabar_scale = intrabar.rolling(20, min_periods=10).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    standardized_intrabar = (intrabar / intrabar_scale).replace(
        [np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan
    ).clip(-4.0, 4.0).fillna(0.0)

    clean_volume = volume.where(volume > 0.0)
    volume_base = clean_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=10).mean().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    relative_volume = (clean_volume / volume_base).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    volume_weight = np.log1p(relative_volume.clip(lower=0.0, upper=5.0)).fillna(0.0)

    return np.sign(gap.fillna(0.0)) * standardized_intrabar * gap_gate * volume_weight


@register_factor
class FundingWedgeConditionedGapFade(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "funding_wedge_conditioned_gap_fade"
    name = "Funding-Wedge Conditioned Gap Fade"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Fades signed overnight-gap retention only for firms in the upper tail "
        "of short-duration working-capital funding fragility."
    )
    window_length = 63
    inputs = [
        "open",
        "close",
        "volume",
        "shortTermDebt",
        "totalDebt",
        "cashConversionCycle",
        "currentRatio",
        "operatingCashFlowGrowth",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        fragility = _funding_fragility(
            data["shortTermDebt"],
            data["totalDebt"],
            data["cashConversionCycle"],
            data["currentRatio"],
            data["operatingCashFlowGrowth"],
        )
        retention = _gap_retention(data["open"], close, data["volume"])

        # Activate smoothly only in the fragile half of the cross-section.
        gate = ((fragility - 0.55) / 0.45).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0).fillna(0.0)
        fade_rank = _neutral_rank(-retention)
        signal = 0.5 + gate * (fade_rank - 0.5)
        return signal.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).fillna(0.5)
programs.name: Funding-Wedge Conditioned Gap Fade
programs.trading_idea: Overnight-to-intrabar confirmation is less reliable for firms whose working-capital cycle is lengthening while debt funding is becoming shorter dated and liquidity is weakening. In that state, an apparently accepted gap can reflect temporary inventory transfer, creditor-sensitive demand, or forced liquidity provision rather than durable information, so the retained gap is faded over the next six bars. Parent A alone identifies a slow-moving balance-sheet vulnerability and Parent B alone cannot distinguish benign information-driven gaps from fragile financing states; their interaction isolates the subset in which price confirmation is most likely to be transient.

It applies that gate to the inverse cross-sectional rank of signed overnight-gap/intrabar-retention strength, weighted by relative volume.

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


@register_factor
class FreshCashFundedGrowthUnderreaction(BaseFactor):
    """Fresh cash-funded growth disclosures that the market has not priced."""

    factor_id = "fresh_cash_funded_growth_underreaction"
    name = "Fresh Cash-Funded Growth Underreaction"
    category = "other"
    description = (
        "Ranks fresh revenue-growth acceleration confirmed by operating-cash-flow "
        "acceleration and restrained asset-growth acceleration, conditional on a "
        "muted three-bar price response."
    )
    window_length = 6
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "revenueGrowth",
        "operatingCashFlowGrowth",
        "assetGrowth",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        revenue_growth = data["revenueGrowth"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        cash_growth = data["operatingCashFlowGrowth"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        asset_growth = data["assetGrowth"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        revenue_accel = revenue_growth - revenue_growth.shift(1)
        cash_accel = cash_growth - cash_growth.shift(1)
        asset_accel = asset_growth - asset_growth.shift(1)

        updated = (
            revenue_accel.notna()
            & cash_accel.notna()
            & asset_accel.notna()
            & (
                revenue_accel.abs().gt(1.0e-12)
                | cash_accel.abs().gt(1.0e-12)
                | asset_accel.abs().gt(1.0e-12)
            )
        )

        # Cash acceleration relative to asset acceleration identifies scalable,
        # internally funded growth rather than mechanically investment-heavy sales.
        fundamental_quality = (
            rank(revenue_accel)
            + rank(cash_accel)
            - rank(asset_accel)
        )

        recent_return = close.pct_change(3).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        muted_reaction = 1.0 - rank(recent_return)
        event_score = (fundamental_quality * muted_reaction).where(updated)

        # Quarterly inputs are point-in-time step functions. Carry a fresh report
        # signal only through the fixed six-bar assimilation interval.
        signal = event_score.ffill(limit=6).fillna(0.0)
        return signal.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).fillna(0.0)

The signal buys such updates only when the stock's immediate three-day reaction is muted, targeting the six-day period in which investors process whether reported growth is cash-realized and capital-efficient. This edge should persist because interpreting the joint cash-flow, investment, and growth disclosure is slower than reacting to the headline sales number; it is falsified if muted high-quality updates do not outperform already-priced updates over the following six bars.

"""Deferred diffusion of cash-validated operating inflections.

Mechanism: revenue and margin acceleration is more credible when operating cash
conversion changes in the same direction.  The first several sessions after a
filing are dominated by mechanical event repricing, so the signal is activated
only after a short refractory period, when analyst-model revision and
institutional implementation should drive continuation.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _filing_change_zscore(field: pd.DataFrame, window: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Standardize sparse point-in-time filing changes using only trailing data."""
    change = field.diff(1)
    scale = change.rolling(window, min_periods=63).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return (change / scale).clip(lower=-5.0, upper=5.0)


def _active_industry_demean(
    values: pd.DataFrame, active: pd.DataFrame, industry: pd.DataFrame
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cross-sectionally remove static-industry means among active names only."""
    labels = industry.iloc[0].astype(object).where(
        industry.iloc[0].notna(), "__UNKNOWN__"
    )
    masked = values.where(active)
    group_mean = masked.T.groupby(labels, sort=False).transform("mean").T
    return (values - group_mean).where(active)


@register_factor
class DeferredCashValidatedOperatingDiffusion(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "deferred_cash_validated_operating_diffusion"
    name = "Deferred Cash-Validated Operating Diffusion"
    category = "other"
    description = (
        "Industry-relative coherent filing innovations in revenue growth, "
        "operating margin, and operating cash conversion, activated only "
        "after a three-bar post-filing refractory period."
    )
    window_length = 252
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "revenueGrowth",
        "operatingMargin",
        "operatingCashFlow",
        "revenue",
        "industry",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        revenue_growth = data["revenueGrowth"]
        operating_margin = data["operatingMargin"]
        revenue = data["revenue"].replace(0.0, np.nan)
        cash_conversion = data["operatingCashFlow"] / revenue

        revenue_z = _filing_change_zscore(revenue_growth, 252)
        margin_z = _filing_change_zscore(operating_margin, 252)
        cash_z = _filing_change_zscore(cash_conversion, 252)

        # All three channels must agree: sales, accounting profitability, and
        # realized operating cash generation identify a credible state change.
        sign_coherent = (
            (revenue_z * margin_z > 0.0)
            & (revenue_z * cash_z > 0.0)
        )
        material = revenue_z.abs().add(margin_z.abs()).add(cash_z.abs()) >= 1.5
        filing_score = (
            revenue_z + margin_z + cash_z
        ).div(3.0).where(sign_coherent & material)

        # Do not trade the noisy initial earnings-event window.  At date t the
        # score uses only a filing observed no later than t-3, then remains
        # active through the following two bars.
        deferred_score = filing_score.shift(3).rolling(3, min_periods=1).sum()
        active = deferred_score.notna() & (deferred_score != 0.0)

        industry_relative = _active_industry_demean(
            deferred_score, active, data["industry"]
        )
        scored = (rank(industry_relative) - 0.5).where(active, 0.0)
        return scored.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Deferred Cash-Validated Operating Diffusion
programs.trading_idea: A revenue-growth and operating-margin inflection is more likely to represent a durable business change when it is also confirmed by improving operating-cash conversion, rather than merely accruals or temporary cost timing. The parent’s negative short-horizon IC suggests that the first few post-filing sessions contain mechanical earnings-event repricing and institutional rebalancing noise; this child deliberately enters only after a three-day refractory period, targeting the subsequent analyst-model and portfolio-update phase within the fixed six-day forecast window. The hypothesis is falsifiable: cash-confirmed coherent updates should have materially stronger positive six-day returns when activated three to five days after disclosure than on disclosure day or for otherwise similar updates lacking cash-conversion confirmation. The edge can persist because translating a multi-statement filing into sustainable margins and cash earnings requires slower fundamental-model revision and mandate-constrained institutional trading.
programs.description: Ranks industry-relative, standardized coherent changes in revenue growth, operating margin, and operating cash conversion. A three-bar post-filing delay excludes the noisy immediate reaction period before holding the filing signal active for three bars.

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _delivery_attention_clock(
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
    eps_surprise: pd.DataFrame,
    eps_estimate: pd.DataFrame,
    revenue_surprise: pd.DataFrame,
    revenue_estimate: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal post-release diffusion score using only previously available bars."""
    safe_close = close.where(close > 0.0)
    ret = safe_close.pct_change().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    volatility = ret.rolling(60, min_periods=20).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)

    eps = eps_surprise.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    eps_base = eps_estimate.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan).clip(lower=0.01)
    eps_z = (eps / eps_base).clip(-5.0, 5.0)

    rev = revenue_surprise.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    rev_base = revenue_estimate.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan).clip(lower=1.0)
    rev_z = (rev / rev_base).clip(-5.0, 5.0)

    prior_eps = eps.shift(1)
    prior_rev = rev.shift(1)
    fresh_eps = eps.notna() & (prior_eps.isna() | ((eps - prior_eps).abs() > 1e-12))
    fresh_rev = rev.notna() & (prior_rev.isna() | ((rev - prior_rev).abs() > 1e-12))
    fresh = fresh_eps | fresh_rev

    same_direction = (eps_z * rev_z) > 0.0
    dual_delivery = ((eps_z + rev_z) / 2.0).where(same_direction, 0.0)
    delivery = eps_z.where(rev_z.isna(), dual_delivery)
    delivery = delivery.where(fresh, 0.0).fillna(0.0)

    # The release is allowed to age for two to five bars before it is traded.
    aged_delivery = (
        delivery.shift(2).fillna(0.0)
        + 0.85 * delivery.shift(3).fillna(0.0)
        + 0.60 * delivery.shift(4).fillna(0.0)
        + 0.35 * delivery.shift(5).fillna(0.0)
    )

    post_release_move = safe_close.pct_change(2)
    move_z = (post_release_move / volatility).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    directional_confirmation = np.tanh((np.sign(aged_delivery) * move_z).clip(-4.0, 4.0))
    directional_confirmation = directional_confirmation.clip(lower=0.0)

    # A modest confirmation is evidence of diffusion; a large move is already absorbed.
    incomplete_adjustment = (1.0 - move_z.abs() / 1.5).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)

    safe_volume = volume.where(volume > 0.0)
    recent_volume = safe_volume.rolling(2, min_periods=2).mean()
    baseline_volume = safe_volume.rolling(30, min_periods=15).mean().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    attention = (recent_volume / baseline_volume).clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0)
    attention_weight = ((attention - 0.8) / 1.2).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)

    score = aged_delivery * directional_confirmation * incomplete_adjustment * attention_weight
    return score.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)


@register_factor
class ConcordantDeliveryAttentionDiffusionClock(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "concordant_delivery_attention_diffusion_clock"
    name = "Concordant Delivery Attention Diffusion"
    category = "sentiment"
    description = (
        "Ranks aged EPS and revenue delivery events whose post-release price "
        "confirmation is incomplete while abnormal volume indicates continuing attention."
    )
    window_length = 60
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "volume",
        "epsSurprise",
        "epsEstimate",
        "revenueSurprise",
        "revenueEstimate",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        score = _delivery_attention_clock(
            data["close"],
            data["volume"],
            data["epsSurprise"],
            data["epsEstimate"],
            data["revenueSurprise"],
            data["revenueEstimate"],
        )
        return rank(score).fillna(0.5)
programs.name: Concordant Delivery Attention Diffusion
programs.trading_idea: A quarterly earnings surprise is more likely to produce durable post-earnings drift when revenue and EPS deliver the same directional message, because investors can update both demand and profitability beliefs rather than dismissing the result as an accounting composition effect. Instead of trading the immediate muted reaction that decays before six days, this child waits for two-to-five-day, low-efficiency directional confirmation accompanied by persistent abnormal volume, which identifies gradual institutional attention diffusion rather than a one-day headline move. The edge can persist because fundamental-model updates and portfolio rebalancing occur across several sessions; it is falsified if concordant delivery events with sustained attention but incomplete price adjustment do not show signed continuation over the next six days.
programs.description: Ranks lagged, concordant EPS-and-revenue surprises after a short post-release confirmation phase. The score is highest when price has moved in the news direction but remains within a modest volatility-scaled range while relative trading volume stays elevated.
